passages.provision_quote: A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enrolled act text creating a faith-based exemption claim/defense against generally applicable laws absent a compelling interest.
Bill details page lists Wesco among the House sponsors of SB 101.
House roll call 305, third reading, single-subject bill; Wesco is the named handler and voted Yea.

rows.reasoning: As a House sponsor of SB 101 (2015), Wesco voted Yea on its single-subject third-reading passage (Yea 63, Nay 31). The enacted text bars government from substantially burdening a person's exercise of religion unless it meets strict scrutiny, creating the faith-based exemption mechanism described by the rung text 'protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs.'
